The only confirmed in-window aggregate figure is from WHO Multi-Country Sitrep #22: 10,556 cases and 162 deaths in Haiti from 1 January to 29 December 2024. This is a full-year figure and cannot be used to isolate Q4 2024 (October–December) counts without a Q3 2024 baseline, which was not retrieved.

The PAHO October 2024 update (phsa-haiti-update-oct2024.pdf) is the most promising Q4-specific candidate but its snippet does not contain extractable case/death counts — it lists cholera as a health threat in narrative context only. Content verification is required before using this as a primary source.

MSPP weekly bulletins for epi weeks 40–52/2024 were not surfaced in either iteration. Haiti's surveillance capacity disruptions due to gang violence may mean some bulletins were not published or are not publicly indexed.
No UNICEF Q4 2024 humanitarian situation reports were retrieved. The BEACON snippet references a UNICEF report covering January–June 2025 (epi weeks 1–25), which is out-of-window.
No ProMED Q4 2024 alerts for Haiti cholera were surfaced. The news_search channel query (q2_004) did not return ProMED results.
No HDX (Humanitarian Data Exchange) structured dataset for Haiti cholera Q4 2024 was surfaced.

50% duplicate rate in iteration 2 (12/24 results) indicates search saturation for the query strategies used — further iterations with the same query patterns would be unlikely to yield new in-window results.

The collection will be limited to: (1) WHO Sitrep #22 full-year 2024 aggregate, and (2) the PAHO October 2024 update as a Q4-specific candidate pending content verification. Subnational, weekly, hospitalization, and locality-level Q4 2024 data remain unconfirmed.

Human review is recommended to manually access: (a) PAHO phsa-haiti-update-oct2024.pdf for Q4 cholera counts; (b) MSPP DELR website (mspp.gouv.ht) for epi week 40–52/2024 bulletins; (c) ReliefWeb UNICEF Haiti sitreps for Q4 2024; (d) HDX Haiti cholera dataset for Q4 2024 time-series data.

iterative_search_queries.query: cholera Haiti cases deaths 2024 site:who.int OR site:paho.org
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: WHO and PAHO are the primary international authoritative sources for Haiti cholera surveillance. Site-scoped search maximizes precision and avoids noise. English-language query targets the main reporting language of these organizations. Covers the full Q4 2024 window via year + month terms rather than rigid date-range strings.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO Disease Outbreak News, PAHO Epidemiological Alerts, PAHO/WHO Haiti cholera situation reports with weekly or cumulative case/death counts
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: who.int or paho.org domain, official situation report or disease outbreak news format, dated within Q4 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: choléra Haïti cas décès 2024 rapport épidémiologique MSPP
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: MSPP is Haiti's national public health authority and the primary source for subnational (département-level) cholera data. French is the official language of Haitian government reporting. This query targets MSPP bulletins which typically include confirmed, suspected, and probable case counts by department and locality.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) weekly epidemiological bulletins, rapports de situation choléra, with departmental breakdowns
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: mspp.gouv.ht domain or MSPP-authored PDF, official bulletin format, subnational (département) data

iterative_search_queries.query: Haiti cholera situation report October November December 2024 site:reliefweb.int OR site:unocha.org
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: ReliefWeb and OCHA aggregate humanitarian situation reports from multiple agencies (UNICEF, WHO, MSF, MSPP) and often host the most current subnational cholera data for Haiti. These reports frequently include département-level case counts, attack rates, and CFRs not available in global dashboards.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: OCHA Haiti Humanitarian Situation Reports, UNICEF cholera updates, ReliefWeb-hosted MSPP or cluster reports with case/death tallies and geographic breakdowns
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: reliefweb.int or unocha.org domain, OCHA/UNICEF/WHO authorship, situation report or flash update format dated Q4 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: Haiti cholera 2024 weekly cases deaths dashboard surveillance data Q4
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Structured databases (WHO Global Cholera Dashboard, HDX, PAHO PLISA) provide machine-readable, time-series cholera data that can validate and cross-check figures from situation reports. ProMED archives provide timestamped outbreak alerts. These are essential for confirming case/death counts and identifying any subnational data not captured in narrative reports.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO Global Cholera and AGE Dashboard, PAHO PLISA database, HDX (Humanitarian Data Exchange) Haiti cholera dataset, ProMED cholera Haiti archive
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Structured tabular or dashboard data with weekly or cumulative counts, sourced from WHO GHO, HDX, or PAHO PLISA, covering Haiti Q4 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: Haiti cholera situation report "October 2024" OR "November 2024" OR "December 2024" PAHO MSPP cases deaths
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Directly targets Q4 2024 month names in combination with PAHO and MSPP to surface situation reports, epidemiological updates, and health cluster sitreps published during or covering October–December 2024. Quoted month strings force temporal precision. Avoids site-scoping to maximize recall across paho.org, iris.paho.org, reliefweb.int, and mspp.gouv.ht simultaneously.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO Haiti health cluster sitreps for epi weeks 40–52/2024, MSPP weekly bulletins for October–December 2024, WHO/PAHO epidemiological updates covering Q4 2024 with case/death counts and departmental breakdowns
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: paho.org, iris.paho.org, or mspp.gouv.ht domain; dated October–December 2024; contains weekly or cumulative case/death figures with subnational breakdown
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: q1_001 — WHO/PAHO site search returned pre-Q4 documents; this query adds explicit month-year strings and broadens to all domains to capture Q4-specific sitreps

iterative_search_queries.query: choléra Haïti octobre novembre décembre 2024 semaine épidémiologique cas décès département
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: French-language query targeting MSPP weekly epidemiological bulletins (bulletins hebdomadaires) for epi weeks 40–52 of 2024. Uses French month names (octobre, novembre, décembre) and 'semaine épidémiologique' (epidemiological week) to match MSPP bulletin titles and PAHO French-language sitreps. Departmental breakdown terms included to surface subnational data.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: MSPP DELR weekly bulletins for epi weeks 40–52/2024 with département-level case/death counts; PAHO French-language Haiti sitreps covering Q4 2024; ReliefWeb-hosted MSPP or health cluster reports in French
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: mspp.gouv.ht domain or MSPP-authored PDF on reliefweb.int/paho.org; French-language bulletin format; subnational (département) data for October–December 2024
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: q1_002 — French MSPP query returned no confirmed Q4 2024 results; this query adds explicit French month names and 'semaine épidémiologique' to improve temporal targeting

iterative_search_queries.query: Haiti cholera UNICEF humanitarian situation report Q4 2024 site:reliefweb.int
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: ReliefWeb hosts UNICEF Haiti humanitarian situation reports that typically include cholera case/death counts and subnational breakdowns. The Q4 2024 UNICEF sitreps (covering epi weeks 40–52) are the most likely source for hospitalization data and département-level figures not available in WHO global dashboards. Site-scoping to reliefweb.int maximizes precision for this document type.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: UNICEF Haiti Humanitarian Situation Reports No. 4–6 for 2024 (covering Q4), OCHA Haiti Flash Updates for October–December 2024, health cluster reports with cholera case/death/hospitalization data by département
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: reliefweb.int domain; UNICEF or OCHA authorship; dated October–December 2024; contains cholera case/death figures with geographic breakdown
iterative_search_queries.previous_iteration_basis: q1_003 — ReliefWeb query returned a 2014 document and a 2025 document; this query adds UNICEF as explicit author and Q4 2024 as explicit time term to improve temporal precision

count_semantics_notes: MSPP typically reports cumulative confirmed + suspected cases separately; always record which classification applies
CFR is calculated on confirmed + suspected combined in most MSPP bulletins — note denominator used
Weekly bulletins may reset or revise prior counts — use most recent bulletin for cumulative totals and flag revisions
Hospitalization figures in Haiti often reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions
Some sources report 'cas vus' (cases seen) vs. 'cas hospitalisés' — distinguish carefully
Deaths may be reported as 'décès communautaires' (community deaths) vs. 'décès hospitaliers' — aggregate both if available
disambiguation_risks: 'AWD' (acute watery diarrhea) may be used as a proxy term for cholera in Haiti before laboratory confirmation — treat as suspected/unspecified unless confirmed
'choléra' in French-language Haitian sources is unambiguous but verify case classification (confirmé vs. suspect)
Cumulative vs. incident counts: MSPP bulletins often report cumulative totals — distinguish from new weekly cases
Département-level vs. national totals: avoid double-counting when aggregating subnational rows
Gang violence and displacement context may affect reporting completeness — note data gaps explicitly
OCV campaign coverage figures should not be confused with case counts

Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) cholera bulletins, situation reports, or surveillance summaries covering Haiti Q4 2024 (October–December 2024).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts by département and commune. French-language bulletins are the primary format.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Haiti cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, or country office bulletins covering 2024-10-01 to 2024-12-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO Haiti Country Office and WHO regularly publish cholera situation reports with case and death counts disaggregated by département, often citing MSPP data. These are high-priority collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti, UN OCHA Haiti, and MSF situation reports or humanitarian updates referencing cholera case counts and deaths in Haiti during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF, OCHA, and MSF publish regular humanitarian situation reports for Haiti that include cholera surveillance data, often with subnational breakdowns and hospitalization figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Platform data, WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), or WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record entries for Haiti cholera in Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global platforms aggregate and independently validate national cholera data. These sources can serve as held-back validation against MSPP and PAHO collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED-mail, HealthMap, or GOARN alerts referencing Haiti cholera cases or deaths during October–December 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED and HealthMap provide independent early-warning signals and can validate or flag discrepancies in official case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints on Haiti cholera epidemiology, case definitions, or AWD surveillance methodology relevant to 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (suspected, probable, confirmed), count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), and Vibrio cholerae strain characteristics used in Haiti surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (e.g., Global Health Observatory, HDX/Humanitarian Data Exchange, ECDC) with Haiti cholera time-series data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases may provide machine-readable cholera counts for Haiti that can contextualize and cross-check extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news sources (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) reporting on Haiti cholera outbreaks, case counts, or deaths during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may contain early outbreak signals, quotes from health officials, or case/death figures not yet reflected in official bulletins, particularly given Haiti's challenging reporting environment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national vs. subnational), or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reports frequently mix cumulative totals with weekly incident counts, and national aggregates may obscure subnational data. Human review is needed to resolve these ambiguities before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) is the primary national authority for Haiti cholera surveillance. MSPP publishes weekly and monthly cholera bulletins (Bulletins Épidémiologiques) with case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations disaggregated by département and commune. PAHO Haiti Country Office also publishes official situation reports citing MSPP data.

PAHO/WHO, UNICEF, UN OCHA, and MSF publish regular Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates. These sources independently aggregate MSPP data and often provide subnational breakdowns, making them suitable for both collection and validation roles. WHO Disease Outbreak News and the WHO Global Cholera Platform are key validation sources.

Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX), WHO Global Health Observatory, and ECDC may host structured Haiti cholera datasets with time-series case and death counts. These machine-readable sources support cross-validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies on Haiti cholera epidemiology provide case definitions, count semantics, and methodological context essential for correct interpretation of surveillance data. PubMed, medRxiv, and Lancet Infectious Diseases are key sources.

Haitian news outlets (Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) and international wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP) may report cholera case counts and deaths citing MSPP or health official statements, providing early signals and corroborating evidence for Q4 2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) cholera bulletins, situation reports, or surveillance summaries covering Haiti Q4 2024 (October–December 2024).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts by département and commune. French-language bulletins are the primary format.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Haiti cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, or country office bulletins covering 2024-10-01 to 2024-12-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO Haiti Country Office and WHO regularly publish cholera situation reports with case and death counts disaggregated by département, often citing MSPP data. These are high-priority collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti, UN OCHA Haiti, and MSF situation reports or humanitarian updates referencing cholera case counts and deaths in Haiti during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF, OCHA, and MSF publish regular humanitarian situation reports for Haiti that include cholera surveillance data, often with subnational breakdowns and hospitalization figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Platform data, WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), or WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record entries for Haiti cholera in Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global platforms aggregate and independently validate national cholera data. These sources can serve as held-back validation against MSPP and PAHO collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED-mail, HealthMap, or GOARN alerts referencing Haiti cholera cases or deaths during October–December 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED and HealthMap provide independent early-warning signals and can validate or flag discrepancies in official case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints on Haiti cholera epidemiology, case definitions, or AWD surveillance methodology relevant to 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (suspected, probable, confirmed), count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), and Vibrio cholerae strain characteristics used in Haiti surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (e.g., Global Health Observatory, HDX/Humanitarian Data Exchange, ECDC) with Haiti cholera time-series data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases may provide machine-readable cholera counts for Haiti that can contextualize and cross-check extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news sources (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) reporting on Haiti cholera outbreaks, case counts, or deaths during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may contain early outbreak signals, quotes from health officials, or case/death figures not yet reflected in official bulletins, particularly given Haiti's challenging reporting environment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national vs. subnational), or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reports frequently mix cumulative totals with weekly incident counts, and national aggregates may obscure subnational data. Human review is needed to resolve these ambiguities before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) is the primary national authority for Haiti cholera surveillance. MSPP publishes weekly and monthly cholera bulletins (Bulletins Épidémiologiques) with case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations disaggregated by département and commune. PAHO Haiti Country Office also publishes official situation reports citing MSPP data.

PAHO/WHO, UNICEF, UN OCHA, and MSF publish regular Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates. These sources independently aggregate MSPP data and often provide subnational breakdowns, making them suitable for both collection and validation roles. WHO Disease Outbreak News and the WHO Global Cholera Platform are key validation sources.

Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX), WHO Global Health Observatory, and ECDC may host structured Haiti cholera datasets with time-series case and death counts. These machine-readable sources support cross-validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies on Haiti cholera epidemiology provide case definitions, count semantics, and methodological context essential for correct interpretation of surveillance data. PubMed, medRxiv, and Lancet Infectious Diseases are key sources.

Haitian news outlets (Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) and international wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP) may report cholera case counts and deaths citing MSPP or health official statements, providing early signals and corroborating evidence for Q4 2024.

count_semantics_notes: MSPP typically reports cumulative confirmed + suspected cases separately; always record which classification applies
CFR is calculated on confirmed + suspected combined in most MSPP bulletins — note denominator used
Weekly bulletins may reset or revise prior counts — use most recent bulletin for cumulative totals and flag revisions
Hospitalization figures in Haiti often reflect CTC (Cholera Treatment Center) admissions, not general hospital admissions
Some sources report 'cas vus' (cases seen) vs. 'cas hospitalisés' — distinguish carefully
Deaths may be reported as 'décès communautaires' (community deaths) vs. 'décès hospitaliers' — aggregate both if available
disambiguation_risks: 'AWD' (acute watery diarrhea) may be used as a proxy term for cholera in Haiti before laboratory confirmation — treat as suspected/unspecified unless confirmed
'choléra' in French-language Haitian sources is unambiguous but verify case classification (confirmé vs. suspect)
Cumulative vs. incident counts: MSPP bulletins often report cumulative totals — distinguish from new weekly cases
Département-level vs. national totals: avoid double-counting when aggregating subnational rows
Gang violence and displacement context may affect reporting completeness — note data gaps explicitly
OCV campaign coverage figures should not be confused with case counts

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) cholera bulletins, situation reports, or surveillance summaries covering Haiti Q4 2024 (October–December 2024).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts by département and commune. French-language bulletins are the primary format.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Haiti cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, or country office bulletins covering 2024-10-01 to 2024-12-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO Haiti Country Office and WHO regularly publish cholera situation reports with case and death counts disaggregated by département, often citing MSPP data. These are high-priority collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti, UN OCHA Haiti, and MSF situation reports or humanitarian updates referencing cholera case counts and deaths in Haiti during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF, OCHA, and MSF publish regular humanitarian situation reports for Haiti that include cholera surveillance data, often with subnational breakdowns and hospitalization figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Platform data, WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), or WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record entries for Haiti cholera in Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global platforms aggregate and independently validate national cholera data. These sources can serve as held-back validation against MSPP and PAHO collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED-mail, HealthMap, or GOARN alerts referencing Haiti cholera cases or deaths during October–December 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED and HealthMap provide independent early-warning signals and can validate or flag discrepancies in official case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints on Haiti cholera epidemiology, case definitions, or AWD surveillance methodology relevant to 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (suspected, probable, confirmed), count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), and Vibrio cholerae strain characteristics used in Haiti surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (e.g., Global Health Observatory, HDX/Humanitarian Data Exchange, ECDC) with Haiti cholera time-series data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases may provide machine-readable cholera counts for Haiti that can contextualize and cross-check extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news sources (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) reporting on Haiti cholera outbreaks, case counts, or deaths during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may contain early outbreak signals, quotes from health officials, or case/death figures not yet reflected in official bulletins, particularly given Haiti's challenging reporting environment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national vs. subnational), or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reports frequently mix cumulative totals with weekly incident counts, and national aggregates may obscure subnational data. Human review is needed to resolve these ambiguities before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) is the primary national authority for Haiti cholera surveillance. MSPP publishes weekly and monthly cholera bulletins (Bulletins Épidémiologiques) with case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations disaggregated by département and commune. PAHO Haiti Country Office also publishes official situation reports citing MSPP data.

PAHO/WHO, UNICEF, UN OCHA, and MSF publish regular Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates. These sources independently aggregate MSPP data and often provide subnational breakdowns, making them suitable for both collection and validation roles. WHO Disease Outbreak News and the WHO Global Cholera Platform are key validation sources.

Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX), WHO Global Health Observatory, and ECDC may host structured Haiti cholera datasets with time-series case and death counts. These machine-readable sources support cross-validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies on Haiti cholera epidemiology provide case definitions, count semantics, and methodological context essential for correct interpretation of surveillance data. PubMed, medRxiv, and Lancet Infectious Diseases are key sources.

Haitian news outlets (Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) and international wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP) may report cholera case counts and deaths citing MSPP or health official statements, providing early signals and corroborating evidence for Q4 2024.
